body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- I moved from GPT-6 Astra to Opus 5.5 because Opus now gives me the finished work I want at lower token rates
- In one same-prompt test, Opus built the better game in both rounds, yet its bill was higher in one round and lower in the other
- Start visible, finished-output work on Opus, but judge the bill per accepted task because a cheaper token does not guarantee a cheaper job

## Astra looked like the Fable-killer, then Opus 5.5 arrived

- When Astra launched, my first reaction was that even Fable was no longer safe
- Since Opus 5.5, my pick for both value and finished output has moved to Opus
- That is my judgment from use, not a controlled test I ran
- In my own use, Opus 5.5 also feels roomier to work in, a felt impression rather than a measured limit
- Launch-day applause, it turns out, comes with a short warranty

## Same prompt, two games

- Moe Lueker gave Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra the exact same prompt twice and allowed no fixes ([Moe Lueker, September 25](https://moelueker.com/blog/claude-opus-5-5-vs-gpt-6-astra))
- Each model started in an empty folder, with Astra in Codex and Opus in Claude Code
- Round 1 was a runner game, and Round 2 was a cozy island builder

![Round 2 island builders from one prompt, with GPT-6 Astra's Tiny Tides next to Claude Opus 5.5's larger, busier island](/images/posts/ai/astra-opus-same-prompt-island.webp)

*Source: [Moe Lueker](https://moelueker.com/blog/claude-opus-5-5-vs-gpt-6-astra) — Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Astra: Same Prompt, Two Games, Real Cost*

- In the runner, Opus added diving, braking, sprinting, checkpoints and its own background music without being asked
- Astra's runner had real art and a parallax background, the best of the GPT-6 builds by the tester's account
- The code gap was 2,405 lines of game code from Opus against 358 from Astra
- On the island, Opus grew the land as you built, added a night mode and rewarded houses placed next to paths
- Astra's island looked plainer than Sol's but offered more tree and house types, and then it stopped
- This is one tester with one build per model per round, so it is a strong example rather than a benchmark
- It still beats comparing two unrelated screenshots and calling it science

## The cheaper token wrote the bigger bill

| Model | Input per 1M tokens | Output per 1M tokens |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Astra | $10 | $50 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 | $20 |

*Standard API rates, Astra short-context tier, checked September 28, 2026: [OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5)*

- Opus lists 60% lower than Astra on both input and output
- Anthropic says Opus 5.5 at medium effort scored 54.6% on FrontierCode, above Astra's best 53.3%, at about a fifth of the cost per task
- That is the maker grading its own launch, so read it as a claim with settings attached
- The same Anthropic page puts Astra ahead on AutomationBench, 41.4% to 40.0%

![Build-turn API cost from the same prompt: Opus 5.5 $15.25 vs Astra $7.09 on the runner, and $5.40 vs $6.88 on the island builder](/images/posts/ai/astra-opus-same-prompt-cost.webp)

*Data: [Moe Lueker](https://moelueker.com/blog/claude-opus-5-5-vs-gpt-6-astra), build turn only at list API rates — chart by HSL*

- On the runner, Opus wrote 256K output tokens to Astra's 36K and cost $15.25 against $7.09
- On the island builder, the bill flipped to $5.40 for Opus and $6.88 for Astra
- Across both games, Opus cost $20.65 and Astra $13.97, about $7 more for the better games
- You pay per task, and Opus decides for itself how much a task deserves
- Unrequested background music is charming until it shows up as output tokens

## How I would split the work

| Job | Start with | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Front end, design, games | Opus 5.5 | Better result in both same-prompt rounds |
| Long back-end debugging | Compare with Astra | The same tester keeps Astra for back end, and one Reddit report below agrees |
| Fixed budget | Set a cap first | Opus may build more than you asked for |

- Put a token or spending cap on long Opus runs before you start
- Track total API spend divided by accepted tasks instead of the rate card
- Keep Astra in the rotation for the problems where Opus stalls

## Community Reactions

- An r/codex author found Opus productive but rated Astra and Fable higher for deep async-runtime design, a real counterexample to "Opus wins everything" ([Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1wpveoe/astra_vs_opus_55_my_impressions_on_hard_project/))
- Another commenter in the same thread said Opus fixed a bot that Astra failed to fix after using a lot of quota, which is one person's experience rather than a measured bill ([Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1wpveoe/astra_vs_opus_55_my_impressions_on_hard_project/))

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q. Is Opus 5.5 always cheaper than Astra?**
  - Per token yes, but per task it depends on how much output Opus decides to write
- **Q. Does one same-prompt test prove Opus is better?**
  - No, it is one tester with one build per model per round, so repeat it on your own work
- **Q. Can I rerun the exact test?**
  - The article does not publish the prompt, so reuse the setup with your own prompt, empty folders and the same effort settings
- **Q. Should I drop Astra entirely?**
  - Not if you do long back-end debugging, where both the tester and a Reddit report still reach for it
title: Why I Switched from GPT-6 Astra to Opus 5.5
description: Why I moved from GPT-6 Astra to Opus 5.5: one same-prompt test gave Opus the better game twice, yet the cheaper-per-token model still ran up the bigger bill once
imageAlt: Notebook showing Astra challenging Fable and Opus 5.5 favored for lower rates and finished work
